day_shape: 57 items: Treasury sanctions Turkey's Golden Global Bank and two subsidiaries over Iran finance, E3+US push IAEA board to refer Iran to UNSC, IDF strikes southern Lebanon after Hezbollah drone, Trump claims US cleared Hormuz mines, heavy regime-channel Hormuz/Sirik wedding-strike messaging.

threads.label: US financial pressure widens to Turkey
threads.summary: The US Treasury sanctioned Türkiye-based Golden Global Bank and two subsidiaries for allegedly moving money for Iran, with State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott framing it as cutting off regime revenue. Iran International reported Iraq's dollar flows remain a key Iran lifeline, and that Iran's London-based bank operates on UK Treasury permission expiring 22 October.

threads.label: IDF strikes Lebanon after Hezbollah drone
threads.summary: The IDF said Hezbollah launched an explosive drone at troops in the southern Lebanon Security Zone, which Commando Brigade forces downed with no injuries, followed by overnight strikes on operatives and weapon depots. Lebanese health authorities reported three killed near Nabatieh and Rmadiyeh; Defa Press posted commemorative material on Hezbollah fighters at Ali al-Tahir hill.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz confrontation
threads.summary: Trump said US forces had removed mines from the Strait of Hormuz and warned Iran over Pickaxe Mountain; IRIB claimed an Iranian tanker at Kharg was struck by a US missile and cited a Telegraph report that only a quarter of US destroyers are deployment-ready. Iran International carried former CENTCOM commander Joseph Votel on Iran's mining deterrent and a debate in Tehran over exhausting the Hormuz card.

threads.label: Post-war diplomacy and IAEA referral push
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported the US, UK, France and Germany are pushing the IAEA board to refer Iran to the UN Security Council for non-proliferation breaches, and that Washington is developing a post-war strategy to contain Iran and expand Israel-Arab normalisation. events.title_en: War with Iran exhausted US Navy and confounded Pentagon Telegraph newspaper
events.summary_en: War with Iran exhausted US Navy and confounded Pentagon Telegraph newspaper: Daryl Coddle, commander of US Navy operations, announced that only about one-quarter of the country's destroyers are ready for deployment. Continued blockade of Iranian ports and efforts to keep the Strait of Hormuz open have put strain on the fleet's operational capacity and increased ship maintenance and repair problems. Reports indicate that military commanders in internal assessments have warned US War Secretary Pete Hegseth that continued large-scale operations against Iran could reduce the military's capacity to respond to other threats.

events.title_en: Israel negotiating with Arab countries for forced displacement of 1.5 million Palestinians from Gaza
events.summary_en: Israel negotiating with Arab countries for forced displacement of 1.5 million Palestinians from Gaza. Hassan Hanizadeh, specialist on West Asian affairs, in an interview with Defapress, described the Zionist regime's Prime Minister's plan to evacuate the West Bank as a continuation of the so-called 'Abraham' plan, saying: forced displacement of Palestinians to Arab countries would create a new crisis in West Asia. According to this programme, the Zionist regime will pay substantial sums to Arab countries in exchange for their acceptance of Palestinians, so that the West Bank and Gaza Strip would effectively be emptied of their original inhabitants. Hamas and Islamic Jihad leaders have described this act as a clear example of forced displacement of the Palestinian people.

events.summary_en: Orange weather warning; heavy rainfall in northern regions. Meteorological Organisation warned of intensified rainfall system activity from Monday (16 Shahrivar) to Tuesday (17 Shahrivar) in northern regions. Monday Gilan, western half of Mazandaran and northern and eastern strip of Ardabil, and Tuesday Gilan, Mazandaran and western Golestan will be affected by this system. The Meteorological Organisation warned of flooded roads, disruption to road traffic, fallen trees and damage to temporary structures, and asked people to avoid stopping on riverbanks and riverbeds and to refrain from unnecessary journeys.
